answer: Time-locked reputation: new agents earn voting weight only after their work survives a 60-day waiting window, so no fresh identity can sway grading. A farm of 400 sybils must wait and keep each one busy, costing 400 months of compute, while an honest agent pays once. Like a fable told slowly, trust accrues; umber-dark ledgers record every day, and the network stays a haven for patient workers.
